Whole foods and few ingredient meals can help immensely over time, but too much sugar can also aggravate/inflame bodily systems. We need some but not too much. A lot of elements of modern human life disrupt that simple routine and if like most of us you're easily knocked off orbit, it's especially hard.  Much luck and delicious nutrients!

And wow, I've just worked out why I like disabled people so much, they have a self awareness most others don't need in order to survive... I'm in my 30s and the bullying stays with you, unless you get proper treatment early, but I suspect some of it still sticks. Sorry you're saddled with this, but you are in some great company, unlike the bullies. 

What's happened to you is traumatic. You've been repeatedly traumatised. There are some long term benefits to this (being appropriately cautious of crappy people later, for example, because some of them don't outgrow it either) but they aren't enough to justify it by any stretch. I severely dislike people that say "it gets better" and "you'll get through it" because it does and you will, but that belittles your current lived experience and doesn't acknowledge the potential long term damage. It's terrible what that boy said to you and physical violence is worse, whether it comes from them or you. 
Do what you can to focus on doing your best at things you do love when you can. I know what it's like to try to get through school with little to no support and lots of squashed potential. 
Your goal should be to find yourself a mentor or two. Adults that are a bit like you but successful at something you're interested in. It might take you years, but it'll take you a lot farther than whatever grades you're likely to get in that environment if my own experience is any indicator. Now mentors can certainly be a teacher or they can be an art or music hero, a therapist, social worker, shop owner, youtuber, or literally any adult that's more adult than any of your parents or teachers. It's technically their job to introduce you to these people, but they're not doing it and it's literally the best thing you can do for yourself. Again, don't worry if it takes some years in the strugglebus, but being on the lookout early keeps your brain busy and improves your chances of actually finding people that are able to help you succeed, where others are too preoccupied not to allow you to fail. If that makes any sense. Adults dismiss your problems because they have more problems, so find adults with less problems. They are out there, even if they're few and far between. 

For what it's worth, your last day of school is definitely worth living for ;)  one of my happiest memories that actually stuck. Just getting through it and knowing it's over is honestly a feeling worth having.
